title: Set up Tracking calls to a phone number on a website

facts.fact: Google states that a call is tracked as a conversion only when it lasts longer than a minimum length the advertiser sets.
facts.quote: tracks a call as a conversion when it lasts longer than a minimum length you set

facts.fact: Google says only one phone number can be tracked on a single page using the default JavaScript tag.
facts.quote: Note: Only one number can be tracked on a single page using the default Javascript tag.

facts.fact: Google says that after linking Google Search Console to Google Ads, the link takes 24 hours to take effect, and call assets must be resubmitted for review.
facts.quote: Links take 24 hours to take effect. You’ll need to resubmit your call assets for review after linking.

facts.fact: Google says the Google tag cannot verify a domain if it is installed through a tag management system such as Google Tag Manager.
facts.quote: Keep in mind that Google tag can't verify your domain if the tag is installed with a tag management system, such as Google Tag Manager.

facts.fact: Google says the phone number entered in Google Tag Manager's website call conversion tag must match the exact digits displayed on the website.
facts.quote: The phone number you enter needs to have the exact digits it has on your website.

facts.fact: Google states that the Google Tag Manager standard website call conversion tag is not compatible with international number formats and can display unintended plus signs on forwarding numbers.
facts.quote: The Google Tag Manager standard website call conversion tag is not compatible with international number formats.

facts.fact: Google says its automated verification system cannot verify a phone number by scanning source code when the website uses Dynamic Number Insertion or third-party call tracking.
facts.quote: If your website uses Dynamic Number Insertion (DNI) or third-party call tracking, Google’s automated verification system can't verify the phone number by scanning your website's source code.

facts.fact: Google does not recommend using Google Tag Manager to install the call conversion tag if the website uses Dynamic Number Insertion or third-party call tracking.
facts.quote: This option isn’t recommended if your website uses Dynamic Number Insertion (DNI) or third-party call tracking.

facts.fact: Google says installing the tag manually is more advanced and recommended only for advertisers comfortable using JavaScript.
facts.quote: This option is more advanced, and is recommended only if you’re comfortable using JavaScript.

facts.fact: Google states that Google forwarding numbers are currently available only in the countries listed on its support page.
